name: What should be included in a commercial construction estimate in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a commercial construction estimate in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a commercial construction estimate in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful commercial construction estimate should be detailed enough to show what is included, what is excluded, and what assumptions were used. At minimum, it should break out demolition, labor, materials, supervision, subcontractors, permits, inspections, equipment, haul-away, temporary protection, and cleanup. It should also identify allowances for items not fully selected yet, such as fixtures, finishes, or specialty equipment. One of the biggest problems in commercial bidding is comparing a vague low bid against a more complete proposal. Owners should look for schedule assumptions, phasing requirements, working-hour restrictions, and who is responsible for design coordination. In Los Angeles-area projects, estimates may also need to reflect local permit costs, city-specific review delays, and any access limitations tied to the site. The clearest estimate is the one that makes hidden costs visible before construction starts. If the proposal leaves out too much, the final price often rises through change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: A commercial construction estimate should clearly list labor, materials, permits, demolition, site protection, supervision, equipment, subcontractors, and exclusions. It should also identify allowances, contingencies, schedule assumptions, and any owner-provided items so the price can be compared accurately across bids.
